Team —

Quick note after this morning's post-sprint review: we surfaced three higher-severity fallout items tied to the inference routing changes (latency spikes for 1% of sessions; cache invalidation mismatch; and a small routing policy regression for dedicated pools). Leadership asked for a concise canary + fallback plan for the QBR (exec will want to see mitigations + rollback criteria).

Action asks (can we please treat these as QBR-ready bullets):
- Kimberly: consolidate the impact window and list the top-5 customer-facing paths affected (include metrics).
- Marissa: propose an exec-level line item for the QBR: who owns the ask and recommended mitigation (A/B canary timeline + SLA caveats).
- Vivek: technical rollback criteria and an emergency fallback flow (what we flip, how long, who gets paged).
- Karthik: any downstream infra dependencies for the rollback (e.g., infra changes that must be coordinated so the rollback doesn't cascade).

I attached a draft canary workbook (2027Q3_canary-plan.xlsx) and a terse QBR inputs doc for edits. Please update by end of day Thursday so I can synthesize for Friday's leadership readout.

Also looping in Elena from NimbleAI — they saw the latency blip in their demo yesterday; Elena, hope it's okay to include your procurement contact in case we need to coordinate timing.

Thanks —
Logan

Impact summary (high level):
- Latency spikes: ~1.1% of sessions experienced >250ms tail increase; correlated with requests hitting variant B (quantized model) during 09:00-10:30 PDT yesterday.
- Cache invalidation: a stale prefix hit surfaced in 3 customer flows — resulted in unexpected model outputs (low severity, but sensitive for a couple of partner integrations).
- Dedicated routing regression: a policy rule mis-match caused routing to fall back to standard-hosted pool for ~120 sessions; this impacted predicted throughput for two reserved tenants.

Top-5 customer paths (I will add metrics & IDs in the workbook):
1) Embeddings pipeline — batch jobs that touch large prefix cache
2) Chat assist — long-context user sessions
3) Re-ranking endpoint — synchronous low-latency calls
4) Dedicated tenant inference path
5) Async bulk transform jobs

I'll annotate severity per customer and flag any that need immediate outreach.

Good start. For the QBR exec slide I want a single-line recommended ask and a contingency bullet. Draft recommendation:

Recommended ask: Pause rollout of variant B for non-critical customers and run a staged canary across 10% of in-region traffic for 48 hours; present performance delta and decision at the July 12 exec checkpoint.
Contingency: If tail latency exceeds +150ms or error rate increases by >0.5% during canary, immediately revert to variant A for all affected routes and trigger postmortem with CS outreach.

I'll take the lead on the exec slide and will need the metrics and rollback wording from Vivek to make the contingency precise. Please push your inputs to the Drive link by EOD Thursday.

Marissa

Adding the technical rollback criteria and quick-runbook here (draft):

Rollback criteria (automated + manual):
- Automated: if 5-minute rolling P95 increases >150ms vs baseline OR request error rate (5m window) increases by >0.5% for canary cohort, automatically terminate canary rollout and route traffic back to variant A via routing-policy toggle.
- Manual: engineering on-call (pager: infra-canary) can trigger rollback if they observe any sustained degradations beyond the automated thresholds.

Emergency fallback flow (3-step):
1) Flip routing-policy flag (runtime toggle) to force variant A for affected regions (expected flip time: 30–90s).
2) Maintain increased logging for 1 hour; capture KV cache snaps for forensic analysis.
3) Post-rollback: create incident page and notify CS/AMs for customer outreach.

Dependencies and notes for Karthik: the routing-policy toggle assumes the latest infra release (build 2027.06.05). If we rollback below that release, we must coordinate DB migration revert windows — I flagged this in the workbook.

I'll add exact metric queries and the runbook steps to the Drive doc.

—Vivek
